scope: Arkansas River near Salida and the Upper Colorado
recommended_first_source: Start with the DORA live outfitter lookup for the hunting or fishing registration, then the CPW river-outfitter list for river-running, then the land authorization that actually covers the water: an AHRA agreement on the Arkansas and a BLM special recreation permit for commercial use of the Upper Colorado. A hit in only one system is not a listing. Do not add a guide or a hull unless a public record names that person or that hull.
highest_priority_permission_question: The nightly DORA extract is labeled public domain, while the real-time outfitter lookup does not restate that license, and the CPW river-outfitter list is silent on reuse. None of those facts authorizes a commercial directory to claim an outfitter listing or to treat a current lookup as the outfitter's consent. The Arkansas River Outfitters Association terms separately prohibit republication of association content.

sample.description: Three CPW river-outfitter business rows cross-checked in the live DORA outfitter lookup. The same two supported rows are the Active OUT sample. Operator names, license numbers, and first-party URLs are withheld.

coverage.population: CPW published river-outfitter businesses statewide, spreadsheet marked updated 2026-06-15 and counted 2026-11-25. Not guides, hulls, launches, or DORA-only fishing outfitters.

Live DORA outfitter lookups for the three CPW-list business names in the river-outfitter sample. Not a river-filtered roster. The statewide nightly count of distinct Active OUT license numbers is recorded on the Information Marketplace coverage row.

Distinct DORA license type OUT numbers with status Active in the nightly Information Marketplace extract queried 2026-11-25. Statewide hunting and fishing outfitter registrations, not a count of Arkansas or Upper Colorado fly businesses. One additional distinct license was Active - With Conditions and is not included in roster_count. Row counts are higher than license counts because some numbers repeat. The live lookup was not re-counted for all 935.

AHRA commercial walk-and-wade authorizations. The October 29, 2025 release says the open permit is one of 15 total authorizations. That figure was not re-counted from a holder list. No public roster of current AHRA commercial contractors was found.
BLM Upper Colorado commercial special-recreation permittees using Pumphouse or the Kremmling-to-State Bridge reach. No permittee roster or count was published on the pages that could be read.
AROA member profile links on one directory page. Membership only. Not a CPW or DORA roster and not a vessel count. Terms prohibit republication of the directory.

sources.scope: State parks, wildlife, fishing, and links into commercial river-outfitter licensing. The homepage does not itself verify an outfitter, a guide, a hull, or a launch.
sources.rights_basis: The privacy and security statement is silent on copyright, redistribution, bulk access, and commercial directory reuse. It says CPW does not warrant accuracy and does not endorse linked products or services.

sources.publisher: Colorado Parks and Wildlife, River Outfitter Licensing Program
sources.role: licensing authority page for river-running outfitters
sources.scope: CPW licenses and regulates river outfitters and says every guide on a regulated river trip must work for a licensed outfitter. The fishing-outfitter step says fishing outfitters must register with DORA and that a DORA fishing outfitter number is required to apply for a river outfitter license. That sentence is placed under the fishing step, not as a statute citation for rafting companies that do not offer fishing. The page also points operators to BLM special recreation permits and to a Forest Service special-use description whose link target is the DORA outfitters homepage, not a Forest Service page. Applications run through the CPW ROL portal. Guide qualification forms are downloads. The guide roster described in program materials is an outfitter upload used by rangers, not a public roster.
sources.credential_holder: River outfitter business. Guides are qualified under the outfitter and are not separately listed on the public license list.
sources.access: Public program page. Application portal is linked at https://cpwrol.state.co.us/login. The public license list is a Google spreadsheet linked from this page.
sources.rights_basis: No commercial-directory grant, attribution requirement, or bulk-license statement is on the program page.
sources.bulk: The linked spreadsheet is a manual public file, not an API.

sources.scope: Statewide list of river-outfitter businesses. Columns are business name, license number, contact name, DBA names, and valid-through year. The first cell reads UPDATED 06/15/26. Export on 2026-11-25 contained 203 business rows: 165 valid through 2026, 18 through 2027, and 20 through 2028. It does not list guides, hulls, launches, waters, or DORA outfitter numbers. It is not a live query.
sources.credential_holder: River outfitter business named on the row.
sources.access: Public Google spreadsheet linked from the CPW program page. Counted from the CSV export.
sources.rights_basis: The spreadsheet and the CPW page that links it state no copyright or commercial-reuse terms. A current row is not authority to claim a directory listing.
sources.bulk: The whole published file can be exported. It is a snapshot, not a feed with a stated update contract.

sources.scope: Privacy, cookies, security, Colorado Open Records Act notice, and an accuracy disclaimer for the CPW website.
sources.rights_basis: Silent on commercial directory reuse and redistribution. States that CPW does not warrant information on the system and does not endorse linked content, products, or services.

sources.publisher: Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies, Division of Professions and Occupations, Office of Outfitters Registration
sources.role: registration authority page for hunting and fishing outfitters
sources.scope: DORA registers outfitters. The page identifies the Office of Outfitters Registration, points to laws and rules, and links licensing services including lookup and roster download. It does not publish a river, water, launch, or hull field. A 2026 rulemaking notice shows the article 12-145 program was still active as of the page checked. Registrations expire March 31 each year according to the applications page.
sources.credential_holder: Registered outfitter, which may be an individual or an entity. Guides are not the registrant unless they themselves are the outfitter.
sources.rights_basis: The program homepage states no commercial-directory grant.
sources.request_process: License lookup, roster download, the Colorado Information Marketplace, and CORA are described on the verification page rather than here.

sources.publisher: Colorado Division of Professions and Occupations
sources.scope: Distinguishes real-time individual primary-source verification, a manual roster download that the page says is not for automated programs, the Colorado Information Marketplace for scheduled API pulls updated nightly, and CORA for other records.
sources.credential_holder: Licensee or licensed entity in a DPO credential type, including Outfitter.
sources.access: Public web page with links to the lookup, the roster generator, and the Information Marketplace dataset.
sources.rights_basis: The page authorizes different access methods. It does not grant a commercial directory the right to present a lookup as state endorsement or as permission for the business to be claimed.
sources.bulk: Automated bulk access is directed to the Information Marketplace. The online roster download is explicitly not for automated programs.
sources.request_process: CORA requests go to the Division email published on this page. Official verification for a short list of non-outfitter professions is a separate email path and does not include outfitters.

sources.publisher: Colorado Division of Professions and Occupations
sources.scope: Individual lookup. The detail view states that it is primary source verification of the license under section 24-34-102, C.R.S. Fields read on detail views: name, city and postal code, license number, DBA, license method, license type, status, original issue date, effective date, expiration date, and public discipline. No water, launch, hull, or guide roster.
sources.credential_holder: The named licensee, person or entity.
sources.access: Public interactive lookup. Three outfitter detail views were opened on 2026-11-25.
sources.rights_basis: The detail view does not restate the Information Marketplace public-domain license and states no commercial-directory grant.
sources.attribution: The detail view attributes the record to the Division as primary source verification.

sources.publisher: Colorado Division of Professions and Occupations
sources.role: manual roster download by license type
sources.scope: Board-and-license-type roster generator. Outfitter is listed as OUT, all statuses, no fee. The page says a larger all-program file and an API are on the Colorado Information Marketplace.
sources.access: Public web form. The outfitter roster file was not downloaded.
sources.rights_basis: The verification page says this download is for a manual pull and is not to be used by automated programs. No commercial-directory grant is stated.
sources.bulk: Manual multi-type download. Automated use is directed elsewhere.

sources.publisher: Colorado Information Marketplace, data from the Department of Regulatory Agencies
sources.role: nightly bulk license extract and field dictionary
sources.scope: All DPO professional and occupational license rows, not a river roster. Outfitter rows use license type OUT. Metadata field names include lastName, firstName, middleName, suffix, entityName, city, state, mailZipCode, licensePrefix, subCategory, licenseNumber, licenseFirstIssueDate, licenseLastRenewedDate, licenseExpirationDate, licenseStatusDescription, specialty, title, degrees, caseNumber, programAction, discipline dates, linkToVerifyLicense, and linkToViewHealthcareProfile. The long description says the file is updated nightly, is for research, and is not guaranteed accurate or complete. It points consumers to the real-time lookup. A 2026-11-25 SODA query of license type OUT returned 2,844 distinct license numbers and 3,188 rows. Distinct Active numbers were 935 (1,014 rows). Distinct Active - With Conditions was 1 (4 rows). Other distinct statuses: Expired 1,857; Revoked 23; Surrendered 20; Voluntary Surrender 6; Cancelled 2. This is not a count of fly-fishing businesses, Arkansas operators, Upper Colorado operators, guides, or vessels.
sources.credential_holder: Each row is a license holder or a repeated row for that license. Outfitter rows may name an entity.
sources.access: Public Socrata dataset and SODA API. DPO describes this as the automated channel, updated nightly.
sources.rights_basis: Dataset metadata license name is Public Domain and licenseId is PUBLIC_DOMAIN. The same metadata says the extract is for research and is not guaranteed. That disclaimer is not a separate commercial-directory permission, and it is not a prohibition stated as a license condition. Public-domain status of the extract is distinct from authority to claim a listing and from the real-time lookup.
sources.attribution: Catalog citation is DORA, Department of Regulatory Agencies. The public-domain label does not state an attribution condition.
sources.bulk: SODA API and file downloads. Nightly automated update. Not the primary-source lookup.
sources.request_process: No additional commercial-permission process is stated. Records outside the published tools are directed to CORA on the verification page.

sources.publisher: Colorado General Assembly, reprinted at colorado.public.law
sources.role: statutory definitions for outfitters and guides
sources.scope: Article 12-145. An outfitter is a person soliciting or providing, for compensation, outfitting services for hunting or fishing on land the person does not own. Outfitting services include transportation by vessel and guiding persons in the take of wildlife. A guide is an individual who accompanies an outfitter's client and is employed or contracted by the outfitter. The public.law copy cites the 2024 CRS PDF and says it is current through Fall 2025, so later 2026 amendments were not re-read from the session laws.
sources.credential_holder: The outfitter registrant. The guide is not given a separate registration in these definitions.
sources.rights_basis: The compilation page states no commercial-directory terms for reuse of the statutory text.

sources.publisher: Colorado General Assembly, reprinted at colorado.public.law
sources.scope: A person shall not act as, advertise as, or represent themselves as an outfitter unless a registration from the division is in effect and in the person's possession. An expired, suspended, or revoked registration does not authorize continued outfitting.
sources.access: Public statutory compilation. Same edition caveat as the definitions section.

sources.publisher: Colorado General Assembly, reprinted at colorado.public.law
sources.scope: Article 33-32. A river outfitter advertises or provides river-running facilities, guide services, or transportation. A river guide is an individual employed for compensation to operate vessels. The compilation's vessel definition includes stand-up paddleboards and excludes single-chambered air-inflated devices that are not paddleboards, and seaplanes. That compilation cites the 2024 CRS PDF. HB 26-1197, effective August 12, 2026, and the November 4, 2026 CPW rule adoption, both address the vessel definition, so this compilation is not a reliable statement of the post-August 2026 statutory text.
sources.credential_holder: River outfitter licensee. Guides and trip leaders are qualified individuals, not the licensee.

sources.role: enacted vessel-registration bill that CPW is using to revise river-outfitter vessel rules
sources.scope: HB 26-1197, Sunset Water Vessel Registration Program, became law. The bill page shows the Governor signed it on May 29, 2026, effective August 12, 2026, chapter 230. CPW's November 4, 2026 adopted Chapter P-3 says the bill revised the statutory vessel definition and that the implementing river-outfitter rules take effect January 1, 2027.
sources.rights_basis: No commercial-directory terms were stated on the bill status page.

sources.role: adopted river-outfitter rules not yet effective
sources.scope: Chapter P-3, River Outfitters, marked approved November 4, 2026. The basis and purpose says the revision implements HB 26-1197 so single-chambered vessels designed to carry one person, including paddleboards and packrafts, may be used on regulated trips. Effective date printed in the document is January 1, 2027. Until then, the CPW program page still labels the operative regulations as effective July 2020.
sources.credential_holder: River outfitter, for the vessels and equipment the outfitter must provide on regulated trips.
sources.rights_basis: The rule PDF states no commercial-directory license.

sources.publisher: Colorado Parks and Wildlife, Arkansas Headwaters Recreation Area
sources.scope: AHRA is a state park along 152 miles of the Arkansas from the Leadville end to Lake Pueblo, with the visitor center in Salida. The page states 102 miles of Gold Medal trout water. It describes visitor access, passes, and river sections. It does not publish a commercial outfitter roster, a launch-by-launch commercial rule, or a hull registry. The visitor center address is a park office, not an operator's departure point.
sources.rights_basis: Uses the CPW website disclaimer. No commercial-directory grant.

sources.scope: October 29, 2025 news release. One walk-and-wade permit was open for a one-year term beginning spring 2026. The release calls that permit one of 15 total walk-and-wade authorizations on the AHRA and says it allows guided walk-and-wade fishing throughout the AHRA. Applications were by invitation email and were due December 5. This is a cap and a vacancy notice, not a roster of current holders and not a boating authorization. The release is dated and CPW warns that news releases can go stale.
sources.credential_holder: The awarded walk-and-wade permit holder, who is not named.
sources.rights_basis: No reuse grant. The page's own disclaimer says dated releases may be inaccurate.
sources.request_process: The release describes an invitation-to-apply email to the AHRA office for that permit vacancy. That is a permit application path, not a data-reuse path.

sources.scope: Defines a commercial use on National Forest System land as a charged entry or participation fee, or a primary purpose of selling a good or service, whether or not profit is intended. The page reached is the commercial recreation-event application path, not a Colorado outfitter roster and not the Pike-San Isabel permittee list. The CPW river-outfitter page's Forest Service link does not point here. It points to the DORA outfitters homepage. No Arkansas or Upper Colorado permittee count was published on the page opened.
sources.credential_holder: Special-use permit holder, when a permit is issued. None is listed here.
sources.access: Public web page. An earlier guessed Forest Service path returned 404.
sources.rights_basis: The page states no copyright notice and no commercial-directory grant.
sources.request_process: Applicants contact the local Forest Service office before applying. That is a permit process, not a data-license process.

sources.publisher: Bureau of Land Management, Kremmling Field Office
sources.scope: Pumphouse Recreation Area is in the Upper Colorado River Special Recreation Management Area and is managed by the Kremmling Field Office. The official page describes it as the most heavily used access on the Upper Colorado between Kremmling and State Bridge and states that the facilities include three developed boat-ramp sites, plus camping and day use. It does not name commercial permittees, hulls, or a fly-fishing outfitter. A direct fetch on 2026-11-25 returned no article body. The description above is from the official page text returned by search extraction the same day. The BLM special-recreation-permit program URL also returned no article body on direct fetch.
sources.access: Public BLM visit page. Permittee roster not found.
sources.rights_basis: No reuse terms were readable on the fetched page.
sources.request_process: BLM special recreation permit applications are a separate land-use process. The program page did not yield a readable permission process for data reuse.

sources.scope: Trade association for commercial whitewater outfitters on the upper Arkansas. The member directory at https://arkansasriveroutfitters.org/outfitters-of-the-aroa/ presented 31 unique member profile links on 2026-11-25. Membership is not a state license, not a hull inventory, and not proof of an AHRA agreement. The directory includes rafting brands and at least one fly-fishing brand. Member names, phones, and addresses were not copied.
sources.rights_basis: The terms say the site content, including text, belongs to the owners, and that copying, redistribution, use, or publication, whether free or for monetary gain, is strictly prohibited. Some content is identified as third-party copyrighted work. Accuracy is not guaranteed.
sources.attribution: Attribution is not offered as permission to republish.
sources.bulk: No bulk license. The member directory is the bulk content the terms cover.

withheld.reason: First-party operator pages, legal names, license numbers, registration cities, and booking URLs stay outside Git. A multi-page operator site counts as one publisher.
